name: gdc-fm-ad
alternateName: Foundation Medicine Adult Cancer Clinical Dataset (FM-AD)
description:
The Foundation Medicine Adult Cancer Clinical Dataset is by a wide margin the largest single cohort indexed here: 18,004 patients across many tumor types, profiled with a targeted DNA panel in a clinical rather than research setting. That scale is genuinely useful for questions about mutation frequency and co-occurrence in a real-world population, which is precisely where research cohorts are least representative.
It is also the clearest case in this corpus of a dataset whose catalog entry invites analyses it cannot support. Vital status is populated for 100% of cases and informative for 0% - every value is "not reported". Race is "not reported" for all 18,004 patients. Every treatment field is empty. Progression and last known disease status are populated for every case and informative for none. A researcher attracted by the sample size will find, after obtaining controlled access to 54,012 files, that no outcome-anchored analysis is possible.
citeAs: The long tail of oncogenic drivers in prostate cancer.

recordSet.name: Clinical variables with measured completeness
recordSet.description: Completeness is measured from the source repository's own records. A field populated entirely with non-answers is reported as populated but not informative, because it blocks an analysis just as surely as an absent field.

supportedQuestions: What are the mutation frequencies and co-occurrence patterns of clinically targeted genes in a large real-world oncology population?
How does the mutational landscape of clinically sequenced patients differ from that of research cohorts such as TCGA?
How common are actionable alterations across tumor types in routine practice?

blockingLimitations.statement: Vital status is populated for 100% of the 18,004 cases and informative for 0%: every value is "not reported". Progression or recurrence and last known disease status show the same pattern - fully populated, entirely uninformative. No outcome endpoint of any kind can be derived.
Every treatment field is empty for every case: prior treatment, treatment type, therapeutic agents, treatment outcome and line of therapy are all at 0% coverage.
Race is recorded as "not reported" for all 18,004 patients. The largest cohort in this corpus contributes nothing to any question about how cancer genomics differs across populations.

inappropriateUses: Any survival, prognostic or outcome analysis.
Any analysis of racial or ethnic differences.
